exceptions.justification: @microsoft/api-extractor is only a link in the dependency path to sprintf-js, which carries advisory GHSA-hp3w-g68c-fv3c (sprintf-js: denial of service through unbounded precision specifiers). The path is @microsoft/api-extractor -> @rushstack/ts-command-line -> argparse@1 -> sprintf-js@1.0.3.
exceptions.alternatives: Replace @microsoft/api-extractor, which the API-contract check is built on; the only fix npm offers is a downgrade of @microsoft/api-extractor to 7.7.8, which would remove the API analysis the check needs.
exceptions.attempted: Ran `npm audit fix` and checked for a newer release of the direct dependency in the path; the installed version is already the latest published one, so none removes the advisory.
exceptions.constraint: @rushstack/ts-command-line (current 5.x) still depends on argparse@1, and argparse@1 on sprintf-js; no patched sprintf-js exists in that range.
exceptions.remediation: Upgrade as soon as @rushstack/ts-command-line drops argparse@1 or a patched sprintf-js is accepted by its range; Dependabot will propose it.
exceptions.residualRisk: Exploiting it needs an attacker-controlled printf-style precision specifier in text that argparse formats. The only caller is api-extractor's own command-line help output, built from fixed strings; the check runs it as a library over this ecosystem's own packages in CI or on a developer machine, never as a service.
exceptions.revisitWhen: @rushstack/ts-command-line stops depending on argparse@1, a patched sprintf-js is published, or the API-contract check stops using api-extractor.
exceptions.ruleBroken: SecurityDeps: no unresolved npm audit finding in what the package installs.
exceptions.whyPreferable: Dropping api-extractor would remove the API-contract check from every package; the exposure above is theoretical.

exceptions.justification: katex carries advisory GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7 (prototype pollution that can bypass trust restrictions, <0.18.2). It is reached only through markdownlint-cli2 -> markdownlint -> micromark-extension-math -> katex@0.16.47.
exceptions.alternatives: Replace markdownlint-cli2; the only fix npm offers is a downgrade of markdownlint-cli2 to 0.0.4, which has no Markdown linting of the current rule set.
exceptions.attempted: Ran `npm audit fix` and checked for a newer release of the direct dependency in the path; the installed version is already the latest published one, so none removes the advisory.
exceptions.constraint: micromark-extension-math requires katex, and markdownlint requires micromark-extension-math; katex 0.18.2 is outside the range the extension accepts for its renderer, and the installed markdownlint-cli2 is already the latest release.
exceptions.remediation: Upgrade as soon as micromark-extension-math or markdownlint accepts a patched katex; Dependabot will propose it.
exceptions.residualRisk: markdownlint imports only the `math` syntax extension to tokenize Markdown; KaTeX is used by the package's separate HTML renderer, which markdownlint never loads, so no math is ever rendered. The tool only reads this ecosystem's own Markdown files in CI or on a developer machine.
exceptions.revisitWhen: A patched katex is accepted by micromark-extension-math, or the Markdown linter is replaced.
exceptions.ruleBroken: SecurityDeps: no unresolved npm audit finding in what the package installs.
exceptions.whyPreferable: Dropping the Markdown linter would remove a docs check for every package; the exposure above is theoretical.

exceptions.justification: smol-toml carries advisory GHSA-r4xh-jqrq-34v2 (quadratic-time parse() because each key line rescans to the end of the document, <=1.8.0). The vulnerable copy is the nested smol-toml@1.8.0 that markdownlint-cli2 installs for itself; knip uses the patched 1.9.0.
exceptions.alternatives: Replace markdownlint-cli2, or wait for it to move to a patched smol-toml; npm offers no fix other than a downgrade of markdownlint-cli2.
exceptions.attempted: Ran `npm audit fix` and checked for a newer release of the direct dependency in the path; the installed version is already the latest published one, so none removes the advisory.
exceptions.constraint: markdownlint-cli2 0.23.3, the latest release, pins smol-toml to a range that resolves to 1.8.0.
exceptions.remediation: Upgrade as soon as markdownlint-cli2 accepts smol-toml 1.9.0 or later; Dependabot will propose it.
exceptions.residualRisk: Exploiting it needs an attacker-controlled TOML document with very many keys; markdownlint-cli2 parses only its own optional TOML configuration file from this ecosystem's repositories, in CI or on a developer machine, and the worst outcome is a slow lint run.
exceptions.revisitWhen: markdownlint-cli2 depends on a patched smol-toml, or the Markdown linter is replaced.

exceptions.whyPreferable: Dropping the Markdown linter would remove a docs check for every package; the exposure above is theoretical.
